Labium dianae sp. nov. was collected in a dry forest (Fig. 2 B) of northwestern Peru (Fig. 2 A), located in the protected area Refugio de Vida Silvestre Laquipampa, in Lambayeque Department. Previously, in South America, Labium was known only from tropical and subtropical rainforests in eastern Brazil (Porter 2003), and the record presented here represents the most northern record of the genus in the continent (Fig. 2 B).
Distribution. Currently known only from the holotype collected in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
